prompt: Users want to sign in with their Google account instead of making a new password.
tells: sign in with their Google account
why: Use OAuth/OpenID Connect with Google as the identity provider.
trap: The ID token is a JWT, but the flow is OAuth.

prompt: A scheduling app needs read access to users' calendars, without ever seeing their passwords.
why: OAuth grants scoped access via tokens the user approves.

prompt: An integration only needs to read contacts, but requests full account access, and users refuse.
trap: Scopes are part of OAuth's design.

prompt: A mobile app can't keep a client secret safe, but still needs to complete an OAuth login.
tells: can't keep a client secret safe
why: Use the authorization code flow with PKCE.
trap: Public clients need PKCE instead of a secret.

prompt: A CI tool needs to read a user's GitHub repositories after they approve it.
why: OAuth: the user grants scoped access to the tool.

prompt: A security audit flags that your OAuth callback doesn't check that the response matches a request your app started.
tells: doesn't check that the response matches
why: Use and verify the state parameter to stop CSRF on the callback.
trap: It's part of the OAuth flow itself.

prompt: Users want to cut off a third-party app's access to their account without changing their password.
tells: cut off a third-party app's access
trap: Delegated access can be withdrawn separately.

prompt: A nightly script with no user present needs an access token to call your API.
why: Use the OAuth client credentials flow.
trap: The resulting token may be a JWT, but the grant is OAuth.
